title: Gradient fallback funnel for multi-arm A/B with fidelity hedging
author: Eleni Kostas
description: Context: We need a safer, low-noise promotion path for multi-arm A/B experiments that mixes shadow verification and canary traffic with adaptive fidelity controls. Existing staged rollouts are brittle when metric signal is noisy across cohorts and when traffic heterogeneity creates false positives that trigger rollbacks. This PR implements a 'gradient fallback funnel': a compact orchestrator stage that gradually introduces live traffic to candidates with a fidelity hedging policy that autoscatters decisions across shadow-check passes and low-fraction canaries before committing. Motivation: reduce unnecessary rollbacks, improve signal-to-noise when A/B arms show small effect sizes, and provide a clear behavioral contract for automatic fallback when telemetry is inconclusive. Changes: 1) rollout/orchestrator/funnel.go: new GradientFunnel controller implementing staged phases - shadow-validate -> low-fraction-safety -> ramp -> commit/rollback. 2) rollout/policies/fidelity_hedge.py: fidelity hedging policy (configurable alpha/beta, shadow passes, entropy threshold). 3) routing/bridge.go: light-weight shadow bridge to mirror traffic with sampling and deterministic session-affinity. 4) telemetry/partitioned_metrics.md: docs for new partitioned SLOs and recommended thresholds. 5) docs/rollout-playbooks.md: new runbook for handling ambiguous signals and operator overrides. 6) e2e/experiment_integration_test.py: new integration test that simulates noisy cohorts and validates fallback behavior. 7) api/rollouts.proto: API extension to expose fidelity parameters and runbook links. Design highlights: - Gradient phases are tunable by duration and fraction; defaults are conservative (2 shadow passes, 0.5% initial ramp). - Fidelity hedging uses a small held-out comparison window and an entropy-based abort when cohorts diverge with high variance. - Automatic fallback paths: fast rollback (immediate revert on catastrophic SLO breach), graceful fallback (move candidate back to shadow only for N minutes), and locked-operator state. - Observability: added debug spans, phased metrics (shadow_passes, hedge_aborts, ramp_progress) and a new dashboard template. Migration: rollout controller is backward-compatible; existing A/B configs can opt into gradient funnel by setting strategy: "gradient_fallback". Linear/Jira: relates to ENG-4820 (rollout safety) and SUP-2110 (customer incident prompting better hedging). Checklist: - [x] Implementation of controller and policy - [x] Unit tests for hedging logic - [x] Integration test with synthetic noise - [x] Docs and runbook - [x] Backwards compatibility and proto bump - [x] Canary in staging for 24h before merge Tests and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky integration test (timeout) which was addressed by increasing test timeouts and adding a deterministic RNG seed. All checks green on the final run. Rollout plan: merge to main, canary in staging for 24 hours targeting internal traffic, enable for one internal product team as opt-in for 2 weeks, then expose to platform config page. Rollback behavior: merged as a safe strategy with clear audit trails and operator overrides. Related: builds on ideas from ENG-3891 (shadow verification) but is intentionally narrower and focused on multi-arm AB patterns.
